title: SLIDERS: Evidence Synthesis with Autonomous Database Reconciliation for Systematic Reviews
claim: Our method beats all retrieval and long-context baselines on every benchmark and stays accurate as corpus size and evidence dispersion grow.
layout: 3 panels: large grouped bar chart left, two stacked line plots right
description: The figure has a large grouped bar chart on the left and two small line plots stacked on the right. The bar chart shows accuracy (%) on six benchmarks: BrowseComp+, WikiCeleb100, FinQ100, FinanceBench, Loong and Oolong. Each benchmark has four bars: RAG in gray, LongRAG in blue, RLM (GPT5) in orange and SLIDERS in dark red. The dark red bars are tallest in every group, and each bar has its value written above it. The legend sits at the left. The top-right plot, titled 'SLIDERS vs. corpus size', plots accuracy against the number of documents (10 to 100) for WikiCeleb100 (blue) and FinQ100 (orange). Both lines stay roughly flat. The bottom-right plot, titled 'BrowseComp+: evidence count', compares SLIDERS (blue) with RLM (red) as the number of evidence-bearing documents grows from 1-3 to 10+. SLIDERS rises to about 100% while RLM stays between 70 and 85%.
caption: SLIDERS, constructs a database from large set of documents and autonomously reconciles inconsistencies through iterative investigation. (left) It outperforms all baselines including RAG, LongRAG and RLM (GPT-5) on all six benchmarks and (right) maintains high accuracy as number of documents and evidence dispersion per question increases.
abstract: Systematic reviews requires comprehensive evidence synthesis from large document corpora to answer targeted research questions and are foundational in finance, social sciences, and other technical fields. Manual construction of evidence tables is labor-intensive, and recent LLM-based assistants relying on embedding or keyword search often fail to meet the coverage standards of systematic reviews. We introduce SLIDERS, a novel LLM-based methodology for automatically assembling evidence tables tailored to research questions for systematic reviews. SLIDERS extracts full-text excerpts that serve as direct evidence or as provenance for structured data. Core to SLIDERS is an autonomous evidence reconciliation coding agent that iteratively writes SQL to analyze and reconcile extracted evidence, bringing together information fragmented across documents, resolving inconsistencies and removing duplicates across records. We evaluate SLIDERS on BrowseComp+, achieving 90% accuracy, and show that it outperforms all baselines on additional benchmarks within the LLM's context window. To assess scalability, we introduce two new evidence-synthesis benchmarks, WikiCeleb100 (3.9M tokens) and FinQ100 (36M tokens), which include follow-up questions beyond the original research query. Although SLIDERS synthesizes evidence knowing only the original question, it answers 78.9% and 55.2% of all questions correctly on WikiCeleb100 and FinQ100, respectively
